title: -na-autoload: exit the main menu after loading (menu-to-session transition)
description:
-na-autoload (thinker fork 2b82af5) successfully loads a savegame - mod_load_daemon returns SAVE_LOAD_VALID (status 0) against a real Autosave_<year>.sav, verified on the gaming host. But the game stays on the main menu, so the loaded state is unreachable.

Clearing *GameHalted is not sufficient. The engine does more of the menu-to-session transition inside load_game (engine.cpp:1057, address 0x5AAAB0) than state loading alone - probably tearing down the menu's own modal loop and entering the main interface. load_game takes (int, int) and addresses saves by slot, which is why it cannot be called directly for an arbitrary path.

Candidate approaches, cheapest first:
1. Identify what load_game does around its call to load_daemon (the call site is hooked at patch.cpp:639, address 0x5AAD7D) and replicate the surrounding steps. Disassembly of 0x5AAAB0..0x5AAD7D would answer it directly.
2. Find the menu's modal loop exit condition and set it alongside GameHalted.
3. Drive the menu with synthetic input instead. xdotool is installed and CAN see the Wine window ('Wine Desktop'), so sending the load-game keystrokes is feasible. Brittle and resolution-dependent, but it needs no engine RE and would unblock unattended runs today.

Approach 3 is the pragmatic unblock; 1 is the correct fix.
acceptance_criteria: Launching with -na-autoload <save> results in a playable in-game session with no human input; na-observations.jsonl shows base.production lines appearing without anyone touching the keyboard
notes:
Starting the QUICK START trace: the label 'QUICK START' does not appear as a string in terranx.exe, in any *.txt in the game directory, or in the 00000409.256 localization resource. So the startup menu is NOT a popp/Script.txt dialog - which rules out the cleanest intervention (intercepting the menu's popp call and answering it programmatically) and means the buttons are drawn from a graphical resource with the dispatch table in code.

Consequence: finding the QUICK START handler needs the menu's click-dispatch code located by structure rather than by string reference. Suggested route: the startup menu is drawn as a Console/Win, and gui.cpp already declares thiscall wrappers for the main-menu class at 0x5FB100 and neighbours (CMAINMENU_ADDSUBMENU_F etc.) - that class is the place to start, since whatever owns the buttons owns their handlers.

Note this does NOT invalidate the strategy in the previous note. Starting a game normally and then swapping state via the replay path is still the right shape; only the means of triggering 'start a game normally' is still open. If QUICK START proves awkward to invoke, any path that establishes a session will do, including a scripted new-game start.
close_reason: SOLVED. -na-autoload reaches a playable session unattended: click QUICK START (opens nothing modal), press Enter to confirm PLANETFALL, then run the engine's own replay/undo load sequence. Verified end to end with no human input - turn 35 from the target save, GameHalted clear, map rendered, no dialog. Key insight: stop constructing the menu-to-session transition and let the engine perform it, then swap state.

title: Verify Steam terranx.exe is Alien Crossfire v2.0
description: Run sha1sum against the Steam Planetary Pack install; want 4b19c1fe3266b5ebc4305cd182ed6e864e3a1c4a (3,084,288 bytes). Thinker refuses any other build. If it differs, the physical ISO plus the official v2.0 patch becomes the primary fixture source. Blocks every game-dependent lane. See docs/headless-harness.md section 2.
notes:
RESOLVED on gaming host (2026-07-29), but NOT by matching the hash.

Steam Planetary Pack (app 2204130), installdir 'Sid Meier's Alpha Centauri':
  terranx.exe  sha1 7bbcc54e64760c11a24f48862f15dbaaeab61435  3,094,576 bytes
  terran.exe   sha1 ca90a0776a5685a01c346e85fd23f3116ece975e  3,201,128 bytes
  PE: i386, 8 sections, link timestamp 1999-12-20 20:30:55 (original Firaxis build, not repacked)

This does NOT match Thinker's documented GOG anchor (4b19c1fe3266b5ebc4305cd182ed6e864e3a1c4a / 3,084,288) - it is 10,288 bytes larger.

It works anyway. Thinker Mod v5.4 is already installed in this directory and has driven a real
game against this exact binary:
  - debug.txt records 'ModVersion Thinker Mod v5.4 (Apr 29 2026)' / 'BinarySize 3094576'
  - saves/auto/ holds a continuous autosave run to Autosave_2234.sav (2026-06-20 19:25-19:56)
Since patch.cpp:218,250 verify original bytes before patching and abort on mismatch, reaching
turn-by-turn play proves every patch site in this build matches v2.0.

Conclusion: the na-8p9 premise ('Thinker refuses any other build') was an overstatement of the
source. Technical.md's own allowance - 'using other official game binaries of the same version
should also work' - is the operative rule, and the Steam build is such a binary. The hash is a
GOG-specific anchor, not a compatibility gate.

Consequence for the fixture (na-dyt): the manifest must record THIS host's hashes as the Steam
provenance line and must not hard-fail on the GOG anchor. Treat the anchor as one known-good
value among several.

Bonus, for na-ie9: it ran under Proton, not bare Wine. Prefix at
~/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/compatdata/2204130/pfx (ModuleName in debug.txt is the Wine
drive mapping S:\common\...). A working prefix already exists to build the Xvfb harness on.
close_reason: Steam build verified compatible empirically: sha1 7bbcc54e... / 3,094,576 bytes differs from the GOG anchor, but Thinker v5.4 patches and plays it (autosaves to year 2234). Fixture source settled as Steam; no ISO needed. See notes.

title: Long-horizon surfaces should issue directives; nothing does yet
description:
Orders.directives exists and the orchestrator accepts, validates and stores what a decision issues, but no decision has ever issued one - every directive measured so far was hand-written into plan.json. The surfaces that should are the low-frequency ones that already reason over a path: faction.tech (fires every 5-10 turns) and faction.se.

The open question is whether a model asked to both decide AND set direction does either worse. That is measurable with the stability harness: run faction.tech with and without the issuing instructions in the prompt and compare stability and choice.
acceptance_criteria: A faction.tech decision issues a directive that a later base.production decision is shown via the multi-hop walk, end to end, with no hand-written plan.json.

title: Verify faction_state metrics live, and re-measure base.hurry with the full chain
description:
na_write_metrics (formerly na_write_faction_state) is built but NOT confirmed against a running game. Two things need checking in one session: (1) the metrics appear on all four surfaces with sane values - energy_income from Faction.energy_surplus_total and military_units from total_combat_units are the two whose engine semantics are assumed rather than verified, and drone_total is a new sweep over the faction's bases that has never run; (2) with base_count reported, the higher-order directive reached at hop 1 stops coming back UNMEASURABLE.

Then re-run the stability harness on base.hurry with the two-directive plan. Expected: setback_turns becomes non-null (it needs energy_income), and the hop-1 strategy directive becomes checkable.

NOTE (na-c17): until recently the adapter wrote these under a faction_state key while the orchestrator reads WorldView.metrics, so the chain was dead and every directive evaluated unmeasurable no matter what was emitted. That is fixed, which means this verification now tests something real - and expectation (2) above was unreachable before, not merely unverified. Also worth watching in the same session: base.hurry observes after mod_base_hurry() runs, so its energy_reserves and minerals_remaining are now the hook's snapshots rather than live fields. Confirm they read pre-decision.
acceptance_criteria: A fresh na-observations.jsonl shows faction_state on all four surfaces; a base.hurry harness run reports zero unmeasurable directives and a non-null setback_turns.

title: Long-horizon directives: measurable strategy that steers tactical decisions
description:
A long-horizon decision (tech, SE, agenda) can reason about a path over many turns, but today its conclusion dies with the response - base.production and base.hurry next turn know nothing about it. Give the LLM's response a way to issue DIRECTIVES that persist and steer later decisions.

The whole design turns on one constraint: a directive may only reference a metric the world view actually reports. That makes it falsifiable instead of vibes - 'keep reserves above 100' can be checked, 'play aggressively' cannot. A directive naming an unreported metric reads as UNMEASURABLE, never as satisfied, because a missing measurement that looks like a passing one is the failure mode that makes the whole mechanism dishonest.

Composes with the doctrine plane (docs/strategy-knowledge.md): doctrine is a curated prior retrieved as grounding, directives are this game's own standing intent.
design: Directives are issued on Orders (the model's response) and injected on WorldView with their live measured value, exactly as grounding is injected. Metrics arrive as an engine-neutral WorldView.metrics dict from the adapter, so the orchestrator never learns where an engine files its economy (invariant 2); metrics.py holds only the vocabulary. increase/decrease comparators capture a baseline at issue time, or they are unmeasurable later.
acceptance_criteria: A directive issued by a faction-level decision is visible, with its current value and satisfied state, in a later base-scope decision record; an unknown or unreported metric is rejected or reported unmeasurable rather than passing.
close_reason: Core mechanism shipped and measured: measurable directives with priorities, value trade-offs, multi-hop entity retrieval and full record instrumentation. base.hurry 0.60 -> 1.00 with 9/10 runs naming the directive. Remaining work split into na-b4v, na-43h, na-mmp.

title: base.hurry is genuinely contested: 0.60 stability at n=10 even fully grounded
description:
base.hurry splits 6/4 between hurry:now and hurry:none over 10 identical prompts on the turn-35 University Base observation (Colony Pod, 5/30 minerals, 81 credits to save 7 turns, 82 in reserve). Utilisation is 0.90, so the brain IS reading the grounding - it just does not resolve the question.

An n=5 run reported 1.00 for the same surface. That was sampling noise, and it is a caution about every 1.00 in the harness: five runs cannot distinguish stable from lucky. Consider raising the harness default.

The hypothesis worth testing is that the missing input is opportunity cost, not rules. 81 of 82 credits is 99% of the treasury, and nothing in the world view says what else that energy could buy or what the faction's income is - base_state carries mineral_surplus but no energy income. A decision about whether a purchase is worth it cannot be made from the price alone.
design: Do NOT chase this with prompt engineering. If the input is genuinely insufficient the fix is a world-view field (energy income, reserve trend, competing sinks); if it is sufficient then 0.60 is the model's honest uncertainty on a close call and the right answer is to measure outcomes (na-6db) rather than consistency.
acceptance_criteria: Either stability rises materially after adding the missing economic inputs, or the surface is documented as a genuine judgement call and routed on outcome evidence instead.
close_reason: Hypothesis confirmed. The surface was short of opportunity cost, not rules: with one priority-7 directive to bank energy credits, base.hurry went from a 6/4 split to unanimous hurry:none over 10 runs, with 9/10 naming the directive as what decided it. Grounding utilisation was already 0.90 before the change, so it was never a retrieval gap. Shipped as the directive mechanism (docs/directives.md); live re-measurement with faction_state tracked in na-b4v.

title: ClaudeBrain sent effort unconditionally, degrading every decision on Haiku 4.5
description:
ClaudeBrain passed output_config={'effort': ...} on every request. Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 4.5 reject the effort parameter with a 400, so invariant 9 (degrade safely) returned the native fallback for every decision. This is a self-hiding outage: the stability harness read five identical fallbacks as 'stability 1.00' and the run looked like a well-behaved model.

Fix: gate effort on a cached models.retrieve capability probe, reading the PER-LEVEL flag rather than the coarse effort.supported - Opus 4.5 reports supported:true and still rejects 'max'. A probe that cannot answer omits effort, because losing effort costs decision quality while raising would cost the decision.
design: Queried, not a hardcoded model list: such a list is wrong the moment a model ships. Cached per instance since the answer cannot change for a fixed model id - base.production fires per base per turn, so an uncached probe would double the round trips per decision.
acceptance_criteria: An unsupported (model, level) pair never reaches messages.parse; a real Haiku 4.5 run through the stability harness reports zero degraded runs.
close_reason: Closed

title: Expand the deterministic tier onto the 21 surfaces with no native AI path
description:
21 of the 77 surfaces (surfaces.NO_AI_PATH) are decisions the native AI NEVER makes - base.abandon, base.disband, base.retool, base.governor_config, base.hq_escape, council.vote, council.buy_vote, diplo.base_swap and the rest.

These must NOT get an LLM tier first. Invariant 9 is degrade safely: a slow, broken or over-budget model returns the safe fallback and the game never stalls waiting on the brain. On these surfaces there IS no fallback - no native choice to revert to - so a model failure stalls or corrupts a turn instead of quietly reverting to a competent default. Putting the brain there first inverts the dependency.

So: build the deterministic tier for them FIRST, in the Thinker fork, as an ordinary mod feature - the same way Thinker already improves production and movement AI. Then add the LLM tier on top, following the established pattern (instrument -> ground -> close the loop -> A/B).

Two reasons this ordering is better than a shortcut:
1. The work is independently useful. A better deterministic tier improves the game whether or not a brain is ever attached, which is also how it gets reviewed and trusted upstream.
2. It gives the LLM something to be measured AGAINST. Without a native answer there is no baseline, so 'the brain decided X' cannot be scored - see na-6db, which needs exactly this baseline to A/B against.

Suggested order within the epic, cheapest and most self-contained first: base.retool and base.governor_config (pure base-local rules), then base.abandon / base.disband (need a value judgement about a base but no diplomacy), then the council and diplomacy surfaces (need cross-faction state and are the least self-contained).

Each child should land as a normal Thinker feature with its own config option defaulting to off, so a stock build is unchanged.
design: Do not batch these. Each surface is a separate engine behaviour with its own correctness question, and a broad change to eleven decision paths at once is unreviewable and unbisectable. One surface, one config flag, one probe, one coverage-table row.
acceptance_criteria: For each surface taken on: a deterministic decision function in the fork, gated by a thinker.ini option defaulting to off; the surface then instrumented with a side-effect-free probe; docs/game-surface.md coverage table updated; and the native answer available as the LLM tier's fallback before any LLM routing is enabled
notes:
Blocks na-6db (outcome measurement): without a deterministic baseline on these surfaces there is nothing to A/B the brain against.

Registry list for reference (surfaces.NO_AI_PATH, 21):
  base.abandon, base.disband, base.governor_config, base.hq_escape, base.retool,
  council.buy_vote, council.vote, diplo.base_swap
  ...and 13 more - query with: python -c "from neural_amplifier import surfaces as S; print(sorted(S.NO_AI_PATH))"

title: Enrich the base.production action space with cost and effect
description:
The action space must carry mineral cost, turns at current surplus, category (unit/facility/project) and a one-line effect for every offered item - not just a display name.

A bare name list is not a decidable comparison. 'Formers' vs 'Scout Patrol' cannot be weighed without cost, and a brain that cannot compare cost will systematically over-pick expensive items. This is the single highest-leverage input for decision quality on this surface (docs/decision-inputs.md section 1.1).

contract.Action is extra=allow, so the extra fields are additive and need no schema change. Ship cost and accumulated minerals separately and let the brain divide - do not pre-compute 'turns remaining' for a partially built item, which is where the arithmetic goes subtly wrong.
acceptance_criteria: Every Action in a base.production world view carries id, name, mineral cost, category and effect; the values are read from the engine, not hardcoded; a world view captured from real play is checked against the engine's own numbers
notes:
VERIFIED against a live game, and it was wrong twice. Fixed in thinker fork.

  - Availability: can_build_unit/can_build are NOT availability tests - they never check tech. 125 options for a turn-35 base, including Alien Artifact. mod_veh_avail / mod_facility_avail are the engine's own tests; same base then offers 8, matching the game's build menu.
  - Cost units: engine cost is in 'rows'; minerals = cost * mod_cost_factor, which varies by faction and difficulty. Base state reports minerals_accumulated in raw minerals, so the world view mixed two units - Colony Pod 'cost 3' against 'accumulated 4' reads as nearly affordable and is actually 33 vs 4. Now normalised and labelled cost_unit=minerals.

Verified output for Gaia's Landing, turn 35: 8 actions - Colony Pod 33, Formers 22, Scout Patrol 11, Synthmetal Garrison 33, Recycling Tanks 44, Recreation Commons 44, Human Genome Project 220, Weather Paradigm 220. Facility effect strings populated from alphax.txt via CFacility.effect.
close_reason: Action space with cost/effect and base state landed in the thinker fork; validation against real play still pending (see notes).

title: Add recent build history to the base.production world view
description:
Record what each base built over the last few turns and include it in the world view, plus whether the current item was chosen by Claude or by the deterministic tier.

BUILT AND THE PREMISE IS VERIFIED; only the live check remains.

Contract: WorldView.history, a list of PriorChoice {turn, item, tier}. Adapter: a four-entry ring buffer per base in scbrown/thinker src/neural.cpp, one entry per turn with last-write-wins (eleven hook sites apply their own answer each turn, so appending per call would fill the window with one turn of churn), and the apply path records tier=llm superseding the deterministic entry for that turn. The prompt tells the brain to treat an unfinished item it chose as the standing answer, and that a deterministic entry is a default to improve on rather than a decision to respect.

The note on this bead said to verify before building, so that was done first, with subagents standing in for the brain. A stable decision cannot demonstrate anything, so the check used a contested one - the base.production world view grounded with four facts, which splits three ways - with history naming the option the brain picks LEAST often. Ten runs per arm on Haiku:

  no history                        continued 0.30
  + three turns of llm history      continued 1.00
  + history, but the case changed   continued 0.10

The third arm is what makes the other two mean anything: history alone cannot separate correctly-continued from anchored-regardless, because nothing in that world view argued for switching. So it changes the case - drones triple and a priority-8 directive caps them - and the brain abandons its own history 9 in 10. Continuity without deference.

STILL OUTSTANDING: the acceptance criterion asks for at least 10 consecutive turns of REAL play showing no oscillation. What was measured is ten independent samples of one synthetic re-decision, which is a different claim. Also the changed arm moves two things at once (metric and directive) so it does not say which did the work. Blocked on na-ie9 for the same reason na-b4v is - it needs a running game.

Harness: scripts/history_stability.py (prompts | score). Written up in docs/decision-inputs.md 2.
acceptance_criteria: World view carries the last N items built or queued for this base, and the tier that chose the current one; verified across at least 10 consecutive turns of real play showing no oscillation between two options
notes:
Instability now measured properly: 5 byte-identical prompts, 4 chose Colony Pod, 1 chose Formers - stability 0.80 (see na-eaa).

This REVISES the earlier note on this issue. I recorded two runs disagreeing and flagged it as suggestive because the prompts differed; the controlled run shows the disagreement was most likely this same 1-in-5 variance rather than the prompt difference. So the effect is real but smaller than implied.

Does recent build history still matter? Probably yes, but the argument is now weaker and should be tested rather than assumed. A 20% flip rate on a decision re-evaluated every turn still means a base changes its mind roughly every five turns, which accumulates nothing - but that is an inference, and na-eaa's harness plus 10 consecutive turns of real play would settle it. Keep at P1 but verify before building.

title: mod_base_build fires twice per base per turn - decide which call is authoritative
description:
Measured in real play on 2026-07-29 (26 observations, turns 2-5, six factions): every (turn, base_id) pair appears EXACTLY TWICE in na-observations.jsonl, and the two calls return different choices. Gaia's Landing on turn 2 produced both 'Scout Patrol' and 'Formers'.

Cause: mod_base_reset is hooked at eleven engine call sites (thinker src/patch.cpp:859-869) - bases_reset, base_production x5, and four BaseWin entry points - and each calls mod_base_build (src/base.cpp:998).

Why this blocks A1 rather than being cosmetic: orchestrator.py owns 'exactly one decision record per decision, on every path'. If the adapter POSTs on every mod_base_build call, one base-turn produces two LLM decisions - double-counted coverage, double-billed tokens, and two contradictory orders for the same slot. The engine is authoritative about what it asks; we have to decide what constitutes one decision.

Thinker fork commit bd1a6ea now records has_gov (mod_base_build's own second parameter) on each observation so the two calls are distinguishable. Next step is to collect a longer sample and determine whether has_gov alone separates them, or whether the call site must also be identified (which would mean passing a discriminator from each patch site).
design: Candidate rules, cheapest first: (1) has_gov distinguishes them cleanly - filter on it; (2) last-call-wins per (turn, base_id), since the final call is what mod_base_change actually applies; (3) identify the call site by passing a constant from each of the eleven patch sites. Prefer (1) or (2) - (3) touches eleven hook sites and couples the adapter to engine layout.
acceptance_criteria: A rule is documented for which mod_base_build invocation is the decision of record; the adapter emits one observation per decision per base-turn, or emits all of them with a field that unambiguously marks the authoritative one; validated against a sample of at least 20 turns
notes:
VERIFIED in real play 2026-07-29, and the original framing was wrong in an important way.

Sample: 50 base.production records, turns 26-34, 38 distinct (turn, base_id) groups.

  call_seq values seen:      1 x38, 2 x10, 3 x2
  calls per (turn,base):     once x28, twice x8, three times x2
  call_seq unique in group:  38 of 38, zero collisions
  records with call_seq==1:  38 - exactly one per distinct base-turn

So gating on call_seq == 1 provably yields exactly one decision per base-turn. A1's
one-paid-call guarantee holds, and the invariant 'exactly one decision record per
decision' is satisfiable.

CORRECTION to the earlier finding. The title says 'fires twice per base per turn'.
It does not - it fires ONE to THREE times, and most often only once (28 of 38 groups).
The first sample happened to catch a turn where duplication was universal, which made
a variable phenomenon look constant.

This matters concretely: any rule of the form 'take the second call' or 'take the last
call' would have MISSED 28 of 38 decisions entirely, because for those groups there is
no second call. call_seq == 1 is correct precisely because it is the only invocation
guaranteed to exist for every base-turn. Had we settled on last-call-wins - which was
the leading theory and sounded principled - A1 would have silently skipped three
quarters of its decisions.
close_reason: Resolved and verified. call_seq is unique within every base-turn group (38/38, no collisions) and exactly one record per base-turn has call_seq==1, so gating on it gives one decision per base-turn. Also corrected the premise: the engine fires 1-3 times, not always twice, and most often once - so a last-call-wins rule would have missed 28 of 38 decisions.

title: K1: Quipu datalinks read path and static briefing
description: Implement Retriever against Quipu: smac shapes, alphax.txt to episode ingester, cached-once static briefing prompt-cached at game start. Exit: a Thinker static briefing is Quipu-sourced. Seam exists in knowledge.py; this fills it. knowledge-architecture.md K1.
close_reason: Landed less the Quipu round-trip. datalinks/ parses alphax.txt deterministically (no model: it is fixed-arity CSV with inline column docs, and a hallucinated tech prerequisite tagged canonical is the worst failure available to us), emits the smac: graph with all three anti-masquerade predicates on every node, and serves a static briefing plus action-space-scoped grounding through the Retriever seam. Verified against a real 1281-line alphax.txt: 88 techs, 133 facilities (50 Disabled), 64 SP rows, 2579 triples round-tripping through rdflib. Three bugs found by checking rather than eyeballing: (1) two facilities have commas inside effect text, so SP detection had to move from row arity to 'last five fields are ints'; (2) Turtle PN_LOCAL forbids '/', so smac:tech/biogen was a parse error that looked perfectly reasonable -- fixed with per-class prefixes and rdflib is now a dev dep gating it; (3) Disable in a preq column means excluded-from-game, not a prerequisite, and treating it as a tech would have invented 50 fake edges. Also: alphax.txt's own header calls the facility column 'Free' (grants the facility free at new bases), not obsoletedBy as knowledge-architecture.md says -- the file wins, noted in rdf.py. Added NA_EXTRACTION_MODEL (default claude-haiku-4-5) as a separate cheaper dial from the brain's, for K3's postgame episode extraction which IS genuine model work. Remaining: load the graph into a running Quipu and serve retrieval from it rather than the parsed structs -- folded into na-6ce (K2). 21 tests against a synthetic excerpt; the real alphax.txt is game data and is never committed.

title: Decide the slot mode and wire manage_player_bases/units
description: Mode B+ is the recommendation: human slot with conf.manage_player_bases and manage_player_units, giving fair rules plus a deterministic tier. Two gaps the LLM must own outright because no AI path runs for a human faction: energy sliders (game.cpp:1908 returns early) and social engineering (faction.cpp:1463 hard-returns). docs/thinker-adapter-notes.md section 5.0.
close_reason: Gate landed in the thinker fork: Config.llm_factions bitmask (default 0 = stock behaviour), llm_endpoint, and llm_enabled() alongside thinker_enabled. Mode B+ recommended and documented at the option in thinker.ini. Verified by MinGW cross-compile to a PE32 DLL. Intercepting an actual decision is A1 (na-61c).

title: A0 spike: log one mod_base_build decision under Wine
description: First real decision point observed. mod_base_build at thinker src/base.cpp:1145 is the cleanest seam: one int in, one int out, self-contained. Depends on the fixture and the harness.
notes:
Hook implemented and shipped: thinker fork commit 78a5af3 adds src/neural.{h,cpp} and calls na_observe_base_production from mod_base_build (src/base.cpp), gated on llm_enabled. Writes one JSON line per decision to na-observations.jsonl in the game directory, with surface_id=base.production, turn, faction, base, and Thinker's native choice. Observation only - native choice still executes, so no behaviour change.

Build and boot are verified: cross-compiles clean under i686 MinGW with -Wall -Wextra -Wshadow, produces PE32 i386, and drives the Steam terranx.exe under Wine 11.9 + Xvfb with the DLL attached (audio confirmed by Steve, so the game genuinely runs).

NOT yet verified: an actual observation line. mod_base_build only fires inside a running game, and a fresh boot sits at the main menu. Producing a line needs either a human to load a game and end a turn, or the -na-autoload flag from na-ie9. That is the only thing standing between here and closing this issue.
close_reason: DONE - observations confirmed in real play 2026-07-29. 26 lines in na-observations.jsonl across turns 2-5 and six factions, each with surface_id=base.production, turn, faction, base, coords, and Thinker's native choice. Full chain proven: fork cross-compiled on Linux, PE32 i386 DLL attached to the Steam Alien Crossfire terranx.exe under Wine, real game, real decision points logged. Note: the na-ie9 dependency was removed as mis-modelled - the spike needed a human to play one turn, not the unattended harness. Follow-up P1 filed: mod_base_build fires twice per base per turn; has_gov now recorded to disambiguate.

title: Wine plus Xvfb headless harness for unattended runs
description: Canned save plus thinker.ini plus -na-autoload / -na-endpoint / -na-exit-turn flags added to cmd_parse. Hard timeout required: Thinker reports fatal errors via MessageBoxA, which under Xvfb hangs forever with nobody to click OK. Run windowed, not fullscreen. docs/headless-harness.md section 3.
notes:
Partially delivered as of 2026-07-29 (commit e78d07a + fork 78a5af3).

DONE - the Wine + Xvfb half:
  - scripts/setup-host.sh installs the i686 cross-compiler, wine, xvfb, cmake>=3.31
  - scripts/play-thinker.sh builds the fork, installs it, and launches, via just thinker-play [headless]
  - Uses its own prefix (~/.local/share/na-wine), never Steam's Proton prefix
  - Verified: the fork boots the Steam terranx.exe under Wine 11.9 + Xvfb, no visible display
  - Correction to an assumption in scripts/setup-environment.sh: a WINEARCH=win32 prefix is NOT
    required on Wine 9+, which runs 32-bit binaries in a default 64-bit prefix via new-wow64.

REMAINING - the menus half, which was always the real blocker (section 3.1):
  - -na-autoload <save>, now best implemented against the in-tree mod_load_daemon(char*, int)
    from upstream f660d9e rather than the raw engine address 0x5A9760
  - -na-exit-turn <n> so an unattended run terminates on its own
  - Fatal-error MessageBoxA suppression only (never blanket-suppress dialogs - invariant 7)
  There is a savegame available to test against: saves/auto/Autosave_2234.sav in the play dir.

title: Build the SMAC game fixture and just game verify
description: Extract the install once to $SMAC_DIR outside the repo; commit a manifest of relative paths plus checksums, never the bytes (copyrighted). Add a just game verify recipe that resolves SMAC_DIR, checks the manifest and reports what is missing. One fixture serves both engines. docs/headless-harness.md section 2.3.
close_reason: Fixture tooling landed: scripts/game_fixture.py (scan/verify, stdlib only), fixtures/smac/{steam-2204130.manifest (1624 files), overlays.tsv, PROVENANCE.md}, just game verify|strict|scan, docs/headless-harness.md 2.3-2.4. Exercised against the real install: clean round-trip, and correct reporting for missing/wrong/contaminated/unreadable/absent-dir. Residual vanilla-restore work tracked in na-8ie; ingest guard in na-yve.

title: Neutralise or declare the fairness handicaps in the adapter
description: Map *DiffLevel and the conf.* values to a concrete per-faction handicap list and populate the world view fairness block. Six entries are difficulty-selected, nine are structural flat is_human branches. Policy is record not neutralise. docs/game-surface.md section 5.
close_reason: Ledger derived, not tabulated: orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/fairness.py computes the fairness block from (slot, difficulty, thinker.ini config) across all 15 entries, each citing its file:line in the fork. Reading the source corrected the game-surface.md table in four places -- tech_cost_factor and content_pop flip sides at Librarian, combat modifiers favour the human not the AI, and unit_support_bonus is inert under shipped defaults. handicap_drift() catches an adapter whose stamp disagrees (missing/unexpected/mislabelled); coverage gained fair_play and structural_handicaps so the claim is measured. 25 new tests. Adapter-side stamping is A1 (na-61c).

title: Evals: keep the committed runs honest as the prompt drifts
description:
evals/runs/ holds the prompts and answers behind every measured number in the docs, and evals/runs/<id>/manifest.json holds a sha256 of each prompt. Nothing checks it.

The failure is quiet and certain: the system prompt changes - it already has, twice - and the committed answers silently become evidence about a prompt that no longer exists, while just eval score keeps printing the same confident table. The docs then quote a number measured against something we no longer ship.

Cheapest fix is a test that regenerates each arm's prompt and compares the hash to the manifest, failing with 'the prompt moved, re-run the eval' rather than pretending. It needs THINKER_DIR to rebuild the world view, so it belongs behind the same skip the quipu tests use rather than in the default lane.

Better but more work: make the prompt reproducible without the sibling checkout by grounding from the committed datalinks/thinker/alphax.ttl instead of the fork's alphax.txt, which would let the check run everywhere.

Not urgent - both runs match their prompts today - but it is the difference between a stale eval announcing itself and a stale eval being believed.

title: Retrieval cost on wide surfaces must be cut option-neutrally
description:
Follow-on from na-373, which refuted rank-then-truncate. Grounding is one fact per option, so any top-k truncation under-explains the options it drops and biases the choice - measured: truncating to the top 4 moved base.production from Network Node 19/20 to Research Hospital 15/20 and cut stability 0.95 to 0.75.

So the cost problem is still open and the shape of an acceptable fix is now known: it has to treat every option the same. Two candidates.

Uniform compression - shorten every fact rather than drop some. Cheapest to try, option-neutral by construction, and measurable with the existing harness.

Two-pass - a cheap fact for every option, rich facts only for a shortlist the brain asks about. Option-neutral in pass one. Costs a round trip on the highest-frequency surface, which is the thing to measure.

Measure with scripts/retrieval_utilisation.py: it already reports utilisation, mean cited, and the choice distribution, and the choice distribution is the half that matters. Acceptance is unchanged from na-373 - utilisation up with NO change to the choice distribution.

title: mdBook docs site
description: The repo had 18 design docs and no way to read them as a site. Set up mdBook with book.toml at the repo root pointing src at docs/ in place, rather than a docs/book/src/ copy: every doc already links its siblings by bare filename and is linked to from README.md and AGENTS.md as docs/<name>.md, so a book-specific source tree would have broken both the ~40 internal cross-references and every GitHub deep link, to render the same output.
close_reason: book.toml at the repo root, src = docs, build-dir = book (gitignored). docs/SUMMARY.md is the TOC across five sections and docs/README.md the index — it also gives the docs/ folder a landing page on GitHub. All 19 chapters render and every local link in the output resolves. Eight links escaping docs/ (six ../VISION.md, two into source files) became absolute GitHub URLs: mdBook rewrites .md to .html relative to the source root, so those resolved outside the book and 404'd. just docs gains build and serve; check is now lint plus build, because a chapter renamed without updating SUMMARY.md passes every markdown rule. CI's lint-markdown lane became docs and builds the book too — it also pinned markdownlint at 0.17.2, a third copy of the version that had drifted from the other two, now 0.23.2 everywhere. mdbook added to setup-environment.sh (release tarball, not cargo install — the lane budget is ~5 minutes) and the CONTRIBUTING tooling table.

title: Directive entity ids are cited as grounding facts and flagged as fabricated
description:
Hank's citation guard fires on 3-4 runs in 5 with 'cited facts that were never offered: fac:the-weather-paradigm'. The model is not hallucinating - it was genuinely shown that id, in a directive's entities list - but the guard reads the offered set only from the grounding block, so a directive entity looks fabricated.

Two id spaces that are deliberately the same (a directive's entities ARE grounding fact ids, which is what makes the multi-hop walk work) but only one of which counts as offered. The guard should treat ids shown in world_view.directives[].directive.entities as offered.

Left as a bug rather than fixed inline because it also inflates a real signal: utilisation counts cited-against-offered, and a citation the guard drops is currently invisible in both directions.
acceptance_criteria: A run where the only 'unoffered' citations are directive entities produces no advisory, and utilisation is unchanged by directives being present.
close_reason: Directive entities now count as offered. hank.CitationGuard reads the offered set as grounding ids UNION world_view.directives[].directive.entities, so citing an id a directive showed is no longer flagged fabricated. The 'none cited' advisory and the utilisation denominator stay scoped to grounding alone — those are statements about retrieval — and a citation only the plan offered lands in the new PlanBlock.entities_cited instead of being silently dropped by summarise. Grounding wins where both offered an id. knowledge.grounded_ids is the single reader of the id-first encoding. 7 tests; 3 of the 4 guard tests fail against the old code, as does the entities_cited one.

title: Metric vocabulary is six faction fields deep; most directives cannot be expressed
description:
metrics.py holds 11 names and the adapter reports 6 faction-level ones. That covers economy and expansion, which is enough for the saving/expansion plans measured so far, but a directive about military posture, terraforming progress, tech position relative to rivals, or diplomatic standing cannot currently be written at all - the name does not exist, so it is refused at issue time.

The honest order of work is adapter first, vocabulary second: a name in the vocabulary that nothing reports produces directives that are permanently unmeasurable, which is the exact failure the closed vocabulary exists to prevent. drone_total is already in the vocabulary and NOT reported - it needs a sweep over bases - so it is the first thing to either emit or remove.
acceptance_criteria: Every name in VOCABULARY is emitted by the adapter, or removed from it.
close_reason: Found a dead seam underneath it: the adapter wrote its measurements under a faction_state key and the orchestrator reads WorldView.metrics, so on a real world view EVERY directive evaluated unmeasurable regardless of what the adapter reported. Both sides were internally consistent and separately tested. Fixed adapter-side per invariant 2 (measurements are adapter-supplied): na_write_faction_state becomes na_write_metrics, emitting the contract key. drone_total is now emitted via a sweep over the faction's bases (drone_total + superdrone_total are per-BASE fields) and turns_to_completion is removed from the vocabulary — the adapter declines to precompute it on correctness grounds and RATE_OF derives it from minerals_remaining anyway. Vocabulary is 10 names, all 10 emitted. Also collapsed the duplicate numbers to one home each, which fixed a latent inconsistency: base.hurry observes after mod_base_hurry() runs, so the record carried the post-purchase energy_credits from faction_state and the pre-decision snapshot from base_state at once. tests/test_metrics_vocabulary.py is the regression guard; two of its tests fail against the old faction_state shape.

title: Directives: attention and override rates need a real game, not a fixture
description:
PlanBlock records in_force/followed/overrode/not_shown per decision, and the harness aggregates them, but every measurement so far is ten replays of ONE captured observation with a hand-written plan. That shows the mechanism works; it says nothing about whether directives help.

What is actually wanted: over a real run, per directive - attention rate (followed/in_force), override rate, and whether the metric moved toward its target. A priority-7 directive overridden on every decision was mispriced. One never overridden may be costing more than it admits. Neither is visible without a game that plays turns.
design: Needs the A1 transport (na-61c) so decisions are applied rather than observed, otherwise a directive cannot influence anything and attention is measuring a counterfactual.

title: A1 adapter must emit WorldView.subjects for base.hurry
description: The subjects field is populated today by the bridge in scripts/decision_stability.py, which maps the adapter's 'item' key. When A1 has the adapter emit the contract directly, it must set subjects itself for any surface that decides ABOUT an entity rather than between entities - base.hurry is the known case. Without it that surface retrieves zero facts, which is what it did until now.

title: Decide the same world view N times to measure decision stability
description:
There is currently no way to tell a considered decision from a coin flip that happens to land on a legal option, because every measurement so far is a single sample.

Two Haiku runs on materially the same base.production world view produced different choices (Formers, then Colony Pod). The prompts were not identical, so that is suggestive rather than conclusive - which is exactly the problem: we cannot currently distinguish 'the model is unstable' from 'the prompts differed'.

Build a small harness that submits the SAME world view N times and reports the distribution of choices, plus the citation sets. Cheap, needs no game running (a captured world view from na-observations.jsonl is enough), and it gives three things nothing else does:
  - a stability number per surface, so 'this surface is decidable from what we send' becomes measurable
  - a regression check on world-view changes: if adding a field makes decisions MORE consistent, that is the field earning its place
  - a way to compare models on the same input without playing a game

Note the interaction with na-61c.2: if instability is real, recent-history context is the fix, and this harness is how you would know it worked.
acceptance_criteria: A script that takes a captured world view and a model, runs it N times, and reports choice distribution and mean utilisation; run against base.production and base.hurry with N>=5 and the results recorded in docs
notes:
FIRST MEASUREMENT TAKEN, controlled this time: five byte-identical prompts, Haiku, base.production at Gaia's Landing turn 35, 8 options, 7 facts offered.

  run 1  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod, formers
  run 2  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod
  run 3  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod
  run 4  unit:1  FORMERS      cited formers, colony-pod
  run 5  unit:0  Colony Pod   cited colony-pod

  stability    0.80  (4 of 5 modal)
  utilisation  0.20 mean (1.4 of 7 facts cited)

So the instability recorded on na-61c.2 is REAL but modest - one flip in five on identical input, not the coin-flip the earlier uncontrolled pair suggested. That earlier observation (Formers vs Colony Pod) is now explained: it was most likely this same 1-in-5, not the prompt differences I hedged about.

Utilisation 0.20 with elimination-citations encouraged, against 0.14 when only the winning option's fact was asked for. Consistent with the na-373 finding that eliminations are real but few.

THE IMPORTANT RESULT is not the number. Run 5 stated 'nearly-complete Colony Pod (18/33 minerals done)'. The world view says minerals_accumulated = 4. It fabricated a state value it had been given correctly - and still reached the right decision, because it took the 15 turns from turns_if_continued rather than deriving it.

That is direct evidence for computing derived values in the adapter, and stronger than the argument that produced turns_if_switched/turns_if_continued in the first place. That change was made because the model got the ARITHMETIC wrong; this shows the precomputed field also insulates the decision when the model misreads the INPUTS. A world view that makes the brain derive things is a world view where a misread propagates into the choice.

title: Measure whether LLM-tier decisions actually produce better outcomes
description:
On base.hurry the brain disagreed with the deterministic tier - it hurried a Colony Pod for 100 of 139 credits to save 15 turns, where Thinker declined. The justification was coherent and numerically grounded. Whether it was RIGHT is unknown, and nothing currently could tell us.

Every claim about decision quality so far is about legality, arithmetic and coherence - all of which are necessary and none of which is the actual goal. A brain that reasons beautifully into a worse position is the failure mode this project most needs to detect, and it is invisible in a single decision record.

What is needed is outcome measurement over a run: play the same save forward under llm_factions=0 and under the brain, and compare trajectories on the measures the game itself keeps - base count, mineral output, tech rate, military strength, faction score. The harness makes this feasible now: autoload is unattended, autosave runs every turn, and the world-view store keeps the bytes for replay.

Note the confound: any comparison must hold the fairness profile fixed, since an AI slot inherits difficulty handicaps a human slot does not (AGENTS.md invariant 6). Comparing an LLM-driven AI slot against a native AI slot at a different difficulty measures the handicap, not the brain.
acceptance_criteria: A repeatable A/B over at least 30 turns from an identical save, reporting the game's own score components for both arms, with the fairness profile recorded and identical across arms
notes:
BLOCKED IN PRACTICE by na-2mn (epic: expand the deterministic tier onto the 21 no-native-AI surfaces). bd will not record a task->epic dependency, so the link is recorded in notes on both issues.

The reason it blocks: an A/B needs a baseline. On the 21 NO_AI_PATH surfaces there is no native decision at all, so 'the brain decided X' cannot be scored against anything. Measurement on the four surfaces already instrumented (base.production, faction.tech, faction.se, base.hurry) can proceed now, because all four DO have a native answer - start there rather than waiting on the epic.

title: Narrow retrieval using the utilisation signal
description:
Grounding utilisation scales inversely with action-space width:

base.production   8 options   7 facts offered   1 cited   utilisation 0.14
base.hurry        2 options   1 fact offered    1 cited   utilisation 1.00

Retrieval fetches one fact per offered action, so a wide surface pays for facts the decision never turns on.

OPTION 1 (rank then truncate) IS REFUTED. Implemented, measured over 20 decisions per configuration on Haiku with a real base.production world view, and reverted. See docs/quipu-integration.md 'Ranking then truncating does not work'.

The rule tried was information value - what a fact adds beyond the option's own name, blind to cost and affordability so retrieval could not bias the choice by desirability. Results:

  all (8 facts)     util 0.22   Network Node 19/20      stability 0.95
  ranked (top 4)    util 0.28   Research Hospital 15/20 stability 0.75

Utilisation rose only because the denominator shrank, and the decision CHANGED and destabilised. The rule also has no predictive power: 15 of 35 baseline citations fell in its top four = 0.43, against 0.50 for pure noise. fac:network-node was cited in 20 of 20 decisions and ranked fifth of eight - the first fact it discards.

The generalisable finding: grounding is one fact per option, so dropping a fact removes the explanation of a specific option rather than removing information, and an unexplained option loses. ANY top-k truncation over a per-option grounding block biases the choice regardless of what it ranks by. Utilisation is a diagnostic, not an optimisation target - maximising it rewards offering less.

Remaining options, re-scoped:
2. Two-pass: cheap facts for every option, rich facts only for a shortlist. Costs a round trip. Still option-neutral in pass one, so it does not have the defect above.
3. Learn from citations (K3, depends on na-bdn).
4. NEW - uniform compression: shorten every fact rather than drop some. Option-neutral by construction, which is the property that matters.

Harness: scripts/retrieval_utilisation.py (prompts | score | predict). The refuted rule lives in it so a replacement can be measured the same way.
acceptance_criteria: Utilisation on base.production rises materially over a sample of at least 20 decisions with no drop in decision quality; the ranking rule is documented and its inputs come from the world view rather than from the graph alone
notes:
PREMISE TESTED AND REFINED - the original framing over-claimed, but the conclusion survives.

The worry was that utilisation 0.14 measured citation CONVENTION rather than waste: a brain that compares 8 options and cites the 1 that won has arguably used all 7 facts, 6 of them to eliminate. So the same decision was re-run asking for citations in three buckets - facts that supported the choice, facts that helped RULE OUT an option, and facts that influenced nothing.

Result:
  DECIDED     unit:colony-pod                         1
  ELIMINATED  fac:recreation-commons                  1
  UNUSED      5 facts, named explicitly by the model  5

So eliminations are real but rare - one, not six - and utilisation rises only from 0.14 to 0.29. Five of seven facts influenced nothing by the model's own account. The waste is real and worth reducing.

Two caveats to carry forward, both of which weaken the number without overturning it:
  - Self-reported 'unused' is weak evidence. A model's introspection about what influenced it is not reliable, and this is the best signal available rather than a good one.
  - Utilisation should COUNT eliminations. Measuring only what supported the winner systematically under-reports, so the instrumentation's definition of 'cited' must include 'helped rule out'. That is a semantics change in what we ask the brain for, not a schema change - Orders.cited already carries a list.

Revised approach: keep ranking as the fix, but do NOT rank by desirability. Ranking cheap-and-soon options first would ground the affordable options better than the expensive ones, which biases the choice through retrieval - a worse failure than wasted tokens, and an invisible one. Rank by expected information value instead: an option whose name does not imply its effect needs a fact; 'Scout Patrol' largely does not.
close_reason: Approach refuted and reverted; the cost problem re-filed as na-vbe with the shape a fix must have. Option 1 (rank then truncate) was implemented and measured over 20 decisions per config on Haiku: utilisation 0.22 to 0.28, but only because the denominator shrank, and the decision changed (Network Node 19/20 to Research Hospital 15/20) with stability falling 0.95 to 0.75. The ranking rule predicts citation worse than chance - 0.43 of citations in its top four against 0.50 for noise - and the one fact cited in 20 of 20 decisions ranked fifth of eight. Generalisable finding recorded in docs/quipu-integration.md: grounding is one fact per option, so top-k truncation removes the explanation of an option rather than removing information, and an unexplained option loses; any such truncation biases the choice whatever it ranks by. Shipped from this work: DatalinksRetriever now emits fact_ids, without which the K1 path could not be cited against at all and utilisation was structurally unmeasurable. Harness kept at scripts/retrieval_utilisation.py.

title: Central mod_popp wrapper: intercept in-game dialogs as decision points
description:
Wrap the engine's dialog function popp(filename, label, a3, pcx_filename, fn) (engine.h:667) so every in-game dialog is visible to the adapter and routable to Claude.

This is invariant 7 made real: 'Intercept in-game dialogs; never blanket-suppress them. They are decision points.' Council votes, diplomacy offers, random events and pact proposals all arrive as popp dialogs, and each is a decision surface the brain should own. Only Thinker's fatal-error MessageBoxA should ever be suppressed.

Precedent exists: Thinker already hooks individual popp call sites - base_production_popp at patch.cpp:681 and BaseWin_staple_popp at 753-754 - so wrapping centrally is the same technique applied once instead of per site. Identify dialogs by (filename, label), which is what the call already passes.

IMPORTANT distinction, do not conflate these:
  - IN-GAME dialogs (events, diplomacy, council) are decisions. Intercept, emit a surface_id, route to the LLM tier where appropriate. Core architecture, and a whole class of surfaces at once.
  - MENU and file-picker chrome (the LOAD dialog) is not a decision, just startup plumbing. Do NOT build automation for it - fix the -na-autoload menu-to-session transition instead so no picker is ever needed. Automating the picker is throwaway work.

Note also that the LOAD picker is not a popp dialog and runs its own message pump, which is why the command channel goes deaf inside it (see na-abc).
acceptance_criteria: A single hook observes every popp dialog with its filename and label; each observed dialog is recorded with a surface_id; a documented allowlist controls which are auto-answered vs routed vs passed through to the human; Thinker's fatal-error MessageBoxA remains suppressed and nothing else is blanket-suppressed

title: Command channel goes deaf inside the engine's modal dialogs
description:
The in-DLL command channel (thinker fork, na_command_tick) is polled from ModWinProc. The engine's modal dialogs - the LOAD file picker among them - run their own message pump, so the window procedure stops being called and the channel stops responding while one is open. Verified: a 'shot' and a 'click' issued with the LOAD dialog open produced no result file at all.

The dialog is drawn INSIDE the game window rather than as a native Windows control (xdotool sees no separate X window for it), so it is not separately addressable from outside either. External input does not reach this game in any case - it reads the mouse through DirectInput under a Wine virtual desktop.

Consequence: automation can open a modal dialog but cannot act inside one. That is enough to reach the LOAD picker and no further, which is exactly one click short of useful.

Candidate fixes:
1. Hook something that runs during modal pumps. popp() and the Console/dialog handlers are the obvious candidates - find one that is unconditionally patched.
2. Avoid dialogs entirely: fix the -na-autoload menu-to-session transition so no picker is ever needed. That is the better goal and is tracked separately as the load_game transition bug.
3. A timer-based tick (SetTimer plus a WM_TIMER handler, or a worker thread) that survives modal pumps. A thread would need care - the engine is not thread-safe.

Approach 2 makes this issue moot for the resume use case, which is the only current consumer. Prefer it.
notes:
Confirmed WORSE than originally described, and now moot for the resume use case.

A worker thread does NOT survive modal dialogs. Input was moved onto a dedicated thread on the reasoning that PostMessage is thread-safe and a thread is independent of the message pump. A heartbeat counter disproved it: the thread ticked normally at the startup screen, froze at the exact instant the picker opened, and never resumed while the process stayed alive. Two plausible causes were tested and eliminated - the picker does not change the working directory, and switching the thread from stdio to Win32 file APIs did not help despite Thinker sharing a single global FileLock with the game (patch.cpp:14-20).

So the constraint is architectural: while a modal dialog is open, NO code of ours runs. Anything needing interaction inside a modal is unreachable.

Moot for resume because na-c9f is solved by never opening a modal (QUICK START instead of LOAD GAME). Keep this open only as a documented limit - if some future surface genuinely needs input inside a modal, the answer is probably to avoid that dialog, not to defeat the pump.

Separate finding worth its own note: in-game input does not reach the engine through posted messages at all. The startup screen and dialogs accept WM_LBUTTONDOWN / WM_KEYDOWN; the map UI does not - it reads DirectInput. So ending a turn cannot be driven from outside the process, which is why an 'observe <base_id>' test hook exists in the DLL.

title: just ingest should refuse a mod-contaminated alphax.txt
description:
The canonical ingester reads $SMAC_DIR/alphax.txt and tags the output canonical. If $SMAC_DIR points at a directory with Thinker installed over it, that file is Thinker's - house-rule data laundered into the canonical smac: graph, violating AGENTS.md invariant 4.

fixtures/smac/overlays.tsv already maps known mod hashes to their source, and scripts/game_fixture.py uses it to detect exactly this. Wire the same check into the ingest path: hash the input, and if it matches a known overlay, abort with a message pointing at just ingest-thinker instead. Cheap, and it closes the hole at the point of harm rather than relying on the operator remembering.
acceptance_criteria: ingest aborts non-zero with an explanatory message when given a file whose sha1 is in overlays.tsv; unit test covers it with no game data in the repo

title: Restore vanilla data files and resolve the 17 unresolved manifest paths
description:
fixtures/smac/steam-2204130.manifest is marked INCOMPLETE: 17 paths held Thinker v5.4 bytes when scanned and carry no vanilla hash - alphax.txt, german/alphax.txt, and 15 basenames/*.txt. Thinker was installed directly into the Steam directory and overwrote them (verified byte-identical to Thinker_v5.4.zip).

Needs a human action in the Steam client: Properties > Installed Files > Verify integrity of game files. That re-downloads tracked files and leaves untracked additions (thinker.dll, thinker.exe, smac_mod/) alone. Then run 'just game scan' to regenerate a complete manifest - it will now succeed without --allow-contaminated.

alphax.txt is the one that matters: 'just ingest' labels it canonical, so ingesting Thinker's copy would mislabel house-rule data as game-canonical (AGENTS.md invariant 4). Do NOT run 'just ingest' against the play directory until this is resolved. basenames/ and german/ are cosmetic and block nothing.
acceptance_criteria: just game scan succeeds with no --allow-contaminated flag; manifest header has no INCOMPLETE block; just game verify passes; just ingest produces a canonical smac: graph from vanilla alphax.txt
notes: Longer-term: $SMAC_DIR should be a pristine tree and the play directory a separate copy with the mod overlaid. See docs/headless-harness.md 2.4 and fixtures/smac/PROVENANCE.md.

title: Supply an embedding model so quipu_context works
description: Filed upstream as scbrown/quipu#53. quipu knot does not embed (only /episode does), --embed-backfill fails with 'No embedding provider configured', and --features onnx supplies the runtime not a model. Needs .bobbin/config.toml with model_path/tokenizer_path plus the all-MiniLM-L6-v2 files. huggingface.co is NOT on the Claude Code cloud Trusted allowlist, so either add it to a Custom allowlist or vendor the model. Exact-match SPARQL grounding is unaffected and works today.

title: Load the datalinks graph into Quipu and serve retrieval from it
description: Finishes K1: DatalinksRetriever currently reads parsed Python structs. Swap the lookup for quipu_context / a SPARQL query against the local store (just quipu-load) behind the same Retriever protocol, so the orchestrator does not notice. Verified reachable: quipu 0.3.11 built with shacl,onnx loads all 2579 triples and answers property-path queries. Overlaps na-6ce (K2); do this first.
close_reason: QuipuRetriever queries a running quipu-server over REST (POST /query, stdlib urllib, no new runtime dep) behind the same Retriever protocol as the struct-backed one, so swapping is a constructor argument. Read-side engine filter is mandatory with no bypass: emission tags appliesToEngine, but if retrieval does not filter on it the tag is decoration -- verified live, glsmac gets 0 hits where thinker gets 1. Non-canonical tiers ride into the prompt. One batched query per decision bounded to the action space, 2s timeout, proxies disabled for loopback, SPARQL literals escaped. BLOCKER FOUND: Quipu implements neither VALUES nor FILTER(?x IN (...)); knowledge-architecture.md, quipu-integration.md and strategy-knowledge.md all specified them. A || disjunction works; all three docs corrected and na-hgd filed. 20 tests, 4 live against quipu 0.3.11. Wired as NA_QUIPU_URL plus 'just quipu-serve'.

title: K6: Hank hot state graph, policy guard and what-if
description: Implement Guard against Hank: hot per-faction COW state graph, deny/warn policies, what-if over the live board. Gated behind new Hank spec FRs. K6, roles c/d/e.
notes:
Role (c) STARTED - the gameplay policy guardrail now has its first policy and is wired into the decision path.

DONE: orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/hank.py CitationGuard. Verifies that facts a brain cited were actually offered and actually resolve, with three distinct advisories because they have three different causes and fixes: fabricated citation (model), offered-but-unresolvable (datalinks integrity), offered-but-uncited (retrieval nobody reads). Verdict is warn, never deny - a suspect justification does not make an order illegal, and role (c) is explicit that legality is the engine's. A throwing resolver returns 'cannot say' rather than a violation. 8 tests.

Wired in service.py _build_guard: on whenever retrieval is, since citation integrity is meaningless without grounding. NA_HANK_GUARD=0 disables. Before this no guard was wired at all, so hank_absent was true on every decision.

This is a LOCAL STAND-IN for Hank's POST /guard, not Hank. The verdict shape and warn/deny semantics are already what that surface returns, so swapping implementations should not change the record.

STILL TO DO: roles (a) engine-mechanics grounding via hank_promote, (b) dev-time guardrail, (d) the hot in-memory game-state graph, (e) what-if over the live board. Also the real policies from the doc - garrison-border-bases, hold-expansion-under-threat, don't-break-a-pact-without-casus-belli - all of which need role (d) first because they reason over board state, not over citations.

title: K2: per-turn Quipu retrieval and budgeting
description: quipu_context plus action-space grounding via one batched SPARQL VALUES query over this turn's action_space, plus hybrid-search tactics k=3 confidence-gated. Token budget: drop tactics before rules. Degradation already handled by the seam. K2.
close_reason: Split: the budgeting half landed, the semantic half is blocked and now has its own bead. Landed: datalinks/budget.py enforces an approximate token ceiling and sheds tactics before rules -- rules are correctness, tactics are optimization, and that ordering is the same precedence the prompt enforces, so the budget cannot invert the trust ordering to save tokens. A single greedy pass in list order would have let a long tactic at the front crowd out a rule behind it, so it fills by precedence class instead, and it keeps scanning past an oversized fact since a later shorter one may still fit. Nothing is dropped silently: the surviving grounding carries an explicit '[N tactics omitted for token budget]' line, because a truncated prompt that reads as complete is the same failure shape as the all-fallback run. Wired as QuipuRetriever(token_budget=N), default 0 = unbounded since the action-space cap already bounds the common case. BLOCKED (na-9tk): quipu_context and quipu_hybrid_search need vectors; quipu knot does not embed, --embed-backfill fails with 'No embedding provider configured', --features onnx gives the runtime not a model, and huggingface.co is not on the cloud Trusted allowlist so the model cannot be fetched from a session. Documented in quipu-integration.md. 12 new tests; 189 pass with a live quipu 0.3.11.

title: K3: learned memory write and recall
description: Postgame extraction to mem: episodes, bitemporal per-game and durable, tactics into the prompt. Exit: a tactic learned in game N surfaces in game N+1. K3.

title: Record a real game into a world-view store
description: Once the fixture and harness exist, run a game with NA_WORLD_VIEW_STORE set and commit the harvested world views as orchestrator fixtures. The store and replay machinery landed with na-10f; this is the half that needs a game.

title: A1: POST the world view and apply Claude's build choice
description: First end-to-end LLM decision in a real game. Wraps mod_base_build to serialize state to the contract, call POST /decide, and apply the returned action. Keep the DLL thin.
notes:
DESIGN SETTLED 2026-07-29. Input requirements are specified per-category in the new docs/decision-inputs.md section 2 - build the world view to that checklist, not ad hoc.

Orchestrator side ALREADY EXISTS: service.py serves POST /decide taking a WorldView and returning
Orders (contract.py). So A1 is DLL-side work only.

Item encoding (thinker src/base.cpp): item_id >= 0 is a unit proto id, item_id < 0 is a facility
with id -item_id, range 1..SP_ID_Last=133. So action ids should be 'unit:<proto>' and
'facility:<id>' - reversible, and it keeps engine ids out of the contract as bare integers.

Action space must be engine-authoritative via can_build(base_id, item) and
can_build_unit(base_id, unit) (base.h:68-69). Never synthesise an option. Enrich each Action with
mineral cost, turns at current surplus, category and a one-line effect - contract.Action is
extra=allow so this needs no schema change. A bare name list is not a decidable comparison and
will bias the brain toward expensive items.

Gate: ask on call_seq == 1 only and reuse the answer for the rest of the base-turn (see
thinker 73fbdbc). One decision, one record, one paid call.

Fallback is the feature, not the error handler: on timeout, transport failure, malformed response,
or an action_id outside the offered space, return native_choice and mark the record degraded.
Wire it from the first commit - invariant 9.

Faction scope: narrow llm_factions from 254 to a single slot. Per the faction-gate commit
rationale, prefer a human slot with manage_player_bases=1 over an AI slot, because an AI slot
silently inherits difficulty handicaps and makes any outcome uninterpretable.

Still to build in the DLL: an HTTP client (none exists - net.cpp is a stub and only user32/gdi32/
winmm/psapi are linked; plan is raw ws2_32 for 127.0.0.1 rather than wininet, which is slow and
quirky under Wine), world-view serialisation, minimal JSON response parsing, and the apply path.

title: Replay mode and determinism diffing
description: Observability step 7. Feed stored world views back through a changed orchestrator with no game running and diff the decisions. Determinism diffing only holds for scripted-brain runs; real-model runs need the weaker assertion of same surfaces fired and same legality.
close_reason: Machinery landed and tested; recording a real game is na-oh5. Dropped the na-04z dependency: the replay path needs stored world views, not an adapter that stamps surface_id -- that was a mis-specified blocker. replay.WorldViewStore is content-addressed by the record's own world_view_hash (the blocker found on starting was that the record carries only the hash and nothing kept the bytes, so a log alone could never be replayed). Two verdicts kept separate: deterministic (exact, scripted only) and consistent (no new degradation, same surfaces fired) -- the trap is a replay where the fallback happens to pick what the brain picked. Wired as NA_WORLD_VIEW_STORE, 'neural-amplifier replay' and 'just replay', plus stored() for fixture harvesting.

title: OpenTelemetry exporter fed from the same emit call
description: Observability step 6. Layer 2. Earns its keep because Quipu and Hank are separate services and without shared trace context a slow turn cannot be attributed. Must be fed from the single DecisionLog.write call, never assembled twice.
close_reason: Layer 2 landed in orchestrator/src/neural_amplifier/telemetry.py. Emitter takes the already-built DecisionRecord and hands the same instance to every sink, so 'assembled once' is structural -- the test asserts object identity, not field equality. DecisionLog is just the first sink and is written first, so an exporter failure still leaves the record of truth on disk; sinks never raise into the decision loop and failures are counted on Emitter.failures and surfaced at GET /health. OtelSink continues the adapter's W3C traceparent rather than starting a new trace (dependency-free strict parser, 10 malformed cases rejected), reconstructs span timing from latency_ms since the decision is already over, sets ERROR status on degradation, and emits the section 6 metrics with a bounded-cardinality attribute subset. Enabled with NA_OTEL=1 and the otel extra. 27 new tests against an in-memory tracer -- no collector, no game. Also fixed a real crash path: _record read world_view.trace.traceparent, which AttributeErrors on a model_copy-constructed view and would stall the game after the decision; now WorldView.traceparent() tolerates both shapes.

title: Adapter stamps surface_id and traceparent on the world view
description: Observability step 5. The adapter's entire telemetry job: two fields on the payload it already sends, plus the fairness block. Export stays in the orchestrator because the DLL must not block the game message pump. docs/observability.md section 4.

title: just docs check is red repo-wide on MD060 table-column-style
description:
Nineteen files — every doc with a table, plus AGENTS.md, README.md and VISION.md — fail 'just docs check' with MD060 'Table pipe is missing space' for the compact style. The pre-push gate 'just check' passes, because its markdownlint hook and the docs recipe do not run the same rule set; only the docs recipe enforces MD060.

That split is the actual problem. AGENTS.md tells you to run 'just check' before pushing and 'just docs build' if docs changed, so a doc change lands green while 'just docs check' has been red for long enough that nobody can tell which failures are new. A gate that is always red is not a gate.

Two ways out and they need a decision, not a sweep: reformat every table to the compact style and keep MD060, or disable MD060 in .markdownlint-cli2.yaml and stop claiming to enforce it. Whichever, the two configs should agree afterwards.
close_reason: Two fixes, because the red gate and the drift were separate problems. (1) markdownlint-cli2 is now pinned to 0.23.2 in both places — a `markdownlint` variable in the justfile and the matching rev in .pre-commit-config.yaml, each pointing at the other. The cause was an unpinned `npx` in the docs recipe floating to 0.23.2 while pre-commit stayed on 0.17.2, so the two gates linted the same files with the same config and different rule sets. (2) All 388 MD060 violations fixed with --fix across 19 files: table separator rows go |---|---| to | --- | --- |, plus one double-space in an empty header cell. Rendering is unchanged. Both `just check` and `just docs check` are green.

title: Ask upstream Quipu for VALUES support
description: Filed upstream as scbrown/quipu#51 (VALUES) and #52 (FILTER IN). quipu 0.3.11 rejects both -- 'unsupported graph pattern' and 'unsupported FILTER expression'. We build a || disjunction instead, which works but is O(n) in query text and gets unwieldy past a few dozen action-space items. Close this when either lands upstream and we can simplify datalinks/quipu.py build_query().
notes:
Second unsupported feature found, same class as VALUES: Quipu rejects FILTER NOT EXISTS.

  query error: unsupported FILTER expression: Exists(Bgp { ... })

Hit while writing a provenance-completeness check ('which typed nodes lack smac:sourcedFrom'). Worked around client-side, which is fine for a lint run at ingest time but means any negation-shaped question has to leave the store. Worth bundling with the VALUES request upstream - both are about expressing 'not in this set'.

title: Parse the remaining alphax.txt sections
description: K1 covers TECHNOLOGY, FACILITIES (incl. secret projects), WEAPONS and DEFENSES. CHASSIS (four name+gender pairs before the numeric fields), UNITS, REACTORS, ABILITIES, TERRAIN, RESOURCEINFO and the SOCIO tables share the file but not the shape, and were skipped rather than half-parsed. Each needs its own row reader plus the smac: classes from knowledge-architecture.md.
notes:
#SOCIO now parsed: 16 social models with effect deltas, emitted as smac:SocialModel with effectText plus structured per-effect predicates. Graph 345 nodes / 3742 facts, provenance 100%. faction.se now has grounding through the same retrieval path as builds - verified live, Free Market resolves to 'economy +2, planet -3, police -5'.

Positional parsing note for whoever touches it: SOCIO is the ONLY section that cannot be read a row at a time. Three header lines, then four groups of four, and a model's category is its group index - nothing in the row names it. Effects are repeated signs, not digits, so -----POLICE is -5.

STILL UNPARSED: #TERRAIN, #RESOURCEINFO, #WORLDBUILDER, #MORALE, #DEFENSEMODES/#OFFENSEMODES, #ORDERS, #CITIZENS, the #SOC* effect-scaling tables, #ENERGY, #TIMECONTROLS.

title: Bounded deny-repair loop for guard denials
description: knowledge-architecture.md specifies deny-violations returned to the model for bounded repair (max 2 retries, then end_turn). Current behaviour is strip-then-degrade, which is correct but gives up a turn the model could have salvaged.

title: Investigate auto_play_callback as the unattended driver
description: 0x50E890, thinker src/engine.cpp:638. Looks like SMAC's own autoplay hook and may answer what occupies the remaining human slot during an unattended run. Cheap to check during the harness work.
close_reason: Negative result: auto_play_callback is NOT the unattended driver. Zero call sites in the fork (engine.cpp:638 declares the pointer, nothing invokes it), and 0x50E890 sits inside a contiguous block of void(int) GUI timer callbacks -- mandate_color 0x50E820, then blink_timer 0x50EA40, blink2_timer, line_timer, turn_timer (its int annotated 'unused'), go_timer. Siblings are patched at GUI offsets and reimplemented in gui.cpp (mod_blink_timer, mod_turn_timer at patch.cpp:445,1158). This is SMAC's attract-mode/animation tick; the name is misleading. headless-harness.md section 7 Q2 updated to say so and to point at load_daemon + cmd_parse + mod_auto_save instead.

title: Fog-gate the AI-to-AI diplomacy feed
description: mod_NetMsg_pop sees all foreign treaty changes; a faction should not know about pacts between factions it has never met. Filter on contact before it enters the world view or it is an information cheat. docs/headless-harness.md section 4.2.
close_reason: Gated orchestrator-side in fog.py. redact() drops any delta naming a faction outside the world view's new contacts list, before the brain call -- a redaction applied after the prompt would be theatre, and the test asserts the brain never saw it. Deltas naming no parties are public news and survive; the viewing faction is implicitly contacted. Removals are counted on the decision record (redacted_deltas) and aggregated in coverage, so a leaking adapter shows up as a number rather than as a suspiciously well-informed run. A world view without contacts sets fog_enforced=false rather than reporting clean -- we cannot distinguish a legitimate delta from a leaked one, so absence of evidence is recorded as such. Contract gained contacts; headless-harness.md section 4.2 documents the gate. 10 tests. Adapter-side filtering at mod_NetMsg_pop is still the right first line and belongs with A1.
